reason: The cited lines show a read-only tool that captures/returns an accessibility snapshot of the current browser page, optionally saving it to a workspace-relative file. They do not show arbitrary host code execution. They do not show delivery to an attacker-readable destination; saving to a local workspace file is not a SINK as defined. The returned page snapshot is web page content and may be attacker-controlled, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The lines do not establish that the current page is non-public, credentialed, localhost/intranet, or otherwise SECRET, only that it is the current page, so SECRET is insufficient.
